instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Believe This with Me
cards.instruction: Recruit someone into treating your impossible explanation as the most useful version of events.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The house is migrating south. Tell the surveyor I'll direct it away from the road.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He says it's subsidence. He's bringing concrete.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You don't immobilize a migrating house halfway out. Ask him to leave a clear route; I'll guide him through it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: His truck's already blocking the road.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then have him drive slowly toward the empty plot. Slowly, please; we're leading a house, not delivering concrete.

beats.text: The office kettle's on strike. Let me handle negotiations; we need tea before the clients arrive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've filled it twice. It still won't boil.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Water isn't pay. Stop refilling it and offer it a place in the meeting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can bring it in, but every chair's taken.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give it mine. Don't invite a negotiating partner and leave it standing on the sideboard. I'll stand.

cards.title: Test the Impossible Claim
cards.instruction: Get someone else to take the first practical step that could prove the bizarre claim true.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This tap gives you whatever you ask for. Ask for tea while I hold a cup; I'll supervise the test.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're not using my good china.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A saucepan will do. We're testing the tap, not the crockery. I'll hold it; you make the request.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll ask, but I'm not tasting anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then request a biscuit. We need a result we can identify by sight. Please don't put your tongue into the experiment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There's an invisible bridge across this ditch. Tap for it with your umbrella; I'll tell you where.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Use your walking stick.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The stick's too sharp. We need a broad contact, not a puncture. Turn your umbrella round and use the handle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll probe, but finding a surface won't prove it can hold us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Once you find it, slide your picnic basket onto it. Keep hold of the handle, please. We're testing a load, not donating lunch.

cards.title: Credit for the Impossible
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge that you understood, predicted, or accepted the impossible truth before anyone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put the date on my staircase drawing before you display it. I drew it last week, before the stairs started floating.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: People can look up and see the staircase now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Observation isn't prediction. The label needs to say what I understood when you were still calling it nonsense.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll put 'well done' beside your name.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put 'predicted', please. We are recording who knew first, not marking my drawing homework.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: In your interview with the talking cupboard, mention that I listened to it for years before it said a word.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's asking for silence. I need you to stop talking while I record it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then write my contribution in the introduction. A proper interview gives the background.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It says your contribution was talking too much.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Quote it exactly, please. Then date those conversations. Readers need to know who was here before it could complain.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Choose the Real Impossibility
cards.instruction: Make someone choose which of two incompatible explanations will govern what everyone does next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put the sofa down. Are we shrinking, or is the room growing? I need your decision before I direct the move.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Whichever gets us through the door.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Those require different methods. Shrinking means outside help; a growing room means move before the door gets farther away. Choose one.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're shrinking. I'll call my brother to take the sofa.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask him to collect us too. Please give him the full job, not just the furniture.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The sandwiches are floating. Is gravity late or has it resigned? Choose, so I can organize service.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Guests arrive in five minutes. I'll start laying the table.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not before we decide. Late means plates underneath; resigned means tether each sandwich. Which method are you preparing for?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Late. We haven't enough string. I'll fetch the side plates.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Deep bowls, please. We've chosen returning gravity; prepare for the whole buffet to arrive together.

cards.title: Act as If It’s True
cards.instruction: Ask for one concrete choice that would only make sense if the impossible premise were true.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The ceiling's hungry. Turn its bowl of porridge upside down; I'll show you how to feed it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's the last of our breakfast.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then divide it first. Half for us, half for the ceiling. Don't tip the serving bowl.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll hold the tray underneath to catch what it drops.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Under the light fitting, please. That's where it dribbles. Keep the tray level; we'll need what's left.

beats.text: Your sister's bringing her future self to dinner. Set two places, please; I'll check them before anyone sits down.

beats.text: Two cards. Put 'future' on the second. I won't have you asking the wrong one how dinner turned out.
